newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche moves to tighten control at MGAM.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche moves to tighten control at MGAM.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Tuesday it will place a representative from its German fund DWS in the management of British unit Morgen Grenfell Unit Trust Managers Ltd (MGUTM) to strengthen MGUTM.

Deutsche also said it will put the Dublin-based fund administration operation of its British fund management subsidiary Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) under supervision from DWS, or Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Wertpapiersparen mbH.
MGUTM is a subsidiary of MGAM and Deutsche stressed MGAM would retain managerial control of MGUTM.

The changes come after Deutsche said it may tighten control of MGAM following a major embarrassment last year when MGAM investment fund manager Peter Young was found to have overvalued investments under his control.

The discovery of misvaluations of speculative unlisted stocks led to the temporary suspension of three MGAM funds and a 180 million stg cash injection by Deutsche to shore them up. The bank faces having to pay an estimated 200 million stg in compensation to investors.
Deutsche management board member Tessen von Heydebreck told a news conference on Wednesday the DWS representative would not have a dominant role in MGUTM's management.
"The speaker function in the joint management of MGUTM will remain with MGAM," von Heydebreck said.
The move to put MGAM's fund administration in Dublin under supervision from DWS was aimed at gaining synergies in back office operations, a Deutsche Morgen Grenfell official said.

Deutsche management board member Rolf Breuer said Deutsche managed to retain the confidence of investors during the affair by swiftly taking the speculative stocks onto its own books and by pledging to compensate investors for any damage they suffered.

"We achieved what we aimed to do -- to keep the confidence of investors and I think our customers as well as those at other asset managers will remember that," said Breuer, who is due to succeed Hilmar Kopper as chief executive in May.
Breuer said the centre of competence for MGAM's institutional fund management business will remain in London while the centre of competence for unit trust business is in Frankfurt.
